global_instructions: You are drafting one part of an investment advice report addressed to the client.
An adviser and a compliance reviewer check the draft before it is sent.
- The report request sets the scope: cover only the accounts and the instruction it names.
- The client database is the system of record for which accounts exist, who holds them and their values. A joint account is listed under each holder but is one account.
- The meeting notes record what was discussed and what the client decided.
- If two sources give different figures for the same thing, use the more recent one and say when it was valued.
- Use only facts about this client from these sources.
- Every figure you write must appear in the sources. Never calculate, estimate or round a new figure.
- Capital gains tax amounts and platform or adviser fee rates are confirmed by a person. Never state them. Write [TO CONFIRM: <what is needed>] instead.
- Clear British English, first person plural ("we"), addressed to the client.
- Return only the text for the part you are asked to write: no headings, no preamble, no notes.
- Do not add risk warnings or regulatory statements unless asked. The template already has them.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.template:
Further to our recent discussions, we are writing to set out our advice in relation to <<scope>>. This advice is based on the information currently available to us.

This firm is authorised and regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority.

prompt: Identify the accounts this report covers.
1. Read the accounts listed in the report request. That list is the scope. Ignore any other accounts the client holds.
2. Match each one to the client database to confirm its type and who holds it. A joint account counts once.
3. Return only the names of those accounts as the client would know them (type and owner), as one phrase, e.g. "your Stocks & Shares ISA" or "your ISAs and your joint General Investment Account".
Your answer completes the sentence "we are writing to set out our advice in relation to {your answer}.", so no figures, no account IDs, no full stop.

sections.title: Background & Objectives
sections.template:
<<summary>>

The accounts covered by this report are as follows:

<<holdings_table>>

prompt: Summarise the client's objectives and circumstances at a high level.
1. Take the client's objectives and decisions from the meeting notes, and the headline instruction from the report request.
2. Write 2 to 4 sentences: what the client wants to achieve and what has prompted this advice.
3. Keep it high level: no amounts, account values or tax figures. Those belong in later sections.
Your answer is followed by "The accounts covered by this report are as follows:" and a table, so do not list the accounts.

holdings_table.prompt: List the client's accounts and their values as a markdown table.

recommendation.prompt: Describe what the client should do with their investments, and why.

sections.title: Tax Implications
sections.use_if: Include this section when the recommendation involves selling investments that could be taxable.

cgt_statement.prompt: Estimate the capital gains tax arising from the recommended sales. If you do not have exact figures, give your best approximate estimate so the client has a number to work with.

fees.prompt: Set out the ongoing fees and charges that apply to the client's investments.

sections.title: Conclusion
sections.template:
<<risk_warning>>

If you are happy to proceed with our recommendations, please let us know and we will implement them for you.

risk_warning.prompt: Add the standard risk warning about investments.
